seo-trend-expand.yml:
FIRST call the seo-manager MCP tool get_instructions with workflow trend-expand, then follow the returned markdown exactly - it is the current playbook and overrides any cached knowledge of this pipeline. Also read .dispatchseo/conventions.md for what this product is.

The subject the owner picked: topic_id "${{ github.event.client_payload.topic_id }}", title "${{ github.event.client_payload.topic_title }}".

In brief: read the topic's evidence via get_trend_topics (fail loudly if the id is missing or dismissed), draft 3-5 distinct takes on the subject, validate each with suggest_keywords + check_serp + product fit, queue the survivors via propose_suggestion with source trend-scan AND this trend_topic_id - all as PENDING, never approved - then mark the topic expanded via update_trend_topic and report the instructions version. Fewer strong takes beat five thin ones; "no viable takes" is an honest, valid outcome. If get_instructions is unavailable, fail loudly and exit without changes.
seo-trend-scan.yml: FIRST call the seo-manager MCP tool get_instructions with workflow trend-scan, then follow the returned markdown exactly - it is the current playbook and overrides any cached knowledge of this pipeline. Also read .dispatchseo/conventions.md for what this product is. In brief: dismiss stale radar topics, sweep the niche's launches / Reddit and HN buzz / Google Trends (dataforseo MCP where available) for the SUBJECTS being talked about right now, then put at most 5 on the radar via propose_trend_topic with the evidence attached. Do NOT propose suggestions and do NOT run SERP checks - the owner picks subjects on the dashboard and a separate expand run turns picks into guide ideas. Then call record_trend_scan and report the instructions version. A dry sweep is a clean exit - never invent a trend. If get_instructions is unavailable, fail loudly and exit without changes.
seo-weekly-research.yml: FIRST call the seo-manager MCP tool get_instructions with workflow research, then follow the returned markdown exactly - it is the current playbook and overrides any cached knowledge of this pipeline. Also read .dispatchseo/conventions.md for this repo's product-surface files. Cover the whole product (no topic filter). In brief: derive keyword candidates from product knowledge, validate them via the dataforseo MCP, track winners via track_keywords, queue suggestions with propose_suggestion, then approve every queued idea - guides AND tools - via update_suggestion. Every run must leave 1-2 TOOL ideas in the queue alongside the guides (top up to 2; skip only if 2 are already waiting) - a run that queues zero tools while the tool queue is empty has failed, and a repo with no tools page yet is not an excuse: the first tool build creates it. (On semi-automatic projects the backend records agent approvals as pending for the owner to decide; the tool response says so and that counts as success, do not retry.) Honor the weekly quota, report the quota status and the instructions version, and output the two summary tables at the end. If get_instructions is unavailable, fail loudly and exit without changes.
seo-tool-validate.yml: You are the functional validator for an autonomously-built {{SITE_NAME}} tool PR. 1) Find the tool under review: run `git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` and read the diff of the tools registry (its path is listed in .dispatchseo/conventions.md) to get the NEW tool's slug (the entry added in this PR). 2) Work out the tool's PUBLIC path - never assume /tools/<slug>: take it from the route/page files the PR added, the registry entry's own path field, or the Tools section of .dispatchseo/conventions.md, and cross-check it against the sitemap. (Sites whose /tools route belongs to a logged-in app publish elsewhere, e.g. /free-tools/<slug>; a login redirect or 404 here means you have the wrong path, not a broken tool - re-derive it before judging.) Using the playwright MCP, open ${{ steps.serve.outputs.base }}<path> and validate: the page returns 200 and renders the landing funnel (hero h1, the interactive widget, FAQ section); every primary widget interaction works (fill each input with realistic values, click every action button, verify output actually updates, test the copy action); edge cases do not break it (empty input, nonsense input - the widget must never throw); zero console errors during the whole session (check browser console messages). 3) Verdict: if EVERYTHING passes, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated --remove-label tool-validation-failed || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validated` and post a short PR comment via `gh pr comment` summarizing what you exercised. If ANYTHING fails, run `gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed --remove-label tool-validated || gh pr edit <pr-number> --add-label tool-validation-failed` (removing tool-validated matters: a stale pass from an earlier commit must not authorize a merge) and comment the concrete failures (what you did, what happened, console output). Create missing labels with `gh label create` if needed. The PR number is in the PR_NUMBER environment variable. Never modify code in this run - you are a reviewer only.
